title: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting - Cultural and Creative Arts - Modelling with Paper Mâché
exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What does the term 'Paper Mâché' literally mean?
questions.explain: The term is French in origin, directly translating to 'chewed paper', which accurately describes the pulped or mashed state of the paper used in this modeling technique.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What is the first step in the process of preparing paper mâché from old newspapers?
options: Painting the newspaper with bright colors.
Tearing the newspaper into tiny bits.
Baking the newspaper in a hot oven.
questions.explain: To prepare paper for pulping, the first logical step is to break down the material by tearing the newspaper into small pieces so they can absorb water easily.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: After tearing the paper into small pieces, the next required step in preparing paper mâché pulp is to:
options: Soak the pieces in water for several hours or days.
Glue the dry pieces directly onto a wall.
Stitch the pieces together with a needle.
questions.explain: Soaking the paper pieces in water softens the fibers, making it possible to mash or pound them into a workable pulp.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which local household equipment is frequently used in schools to pound soaked paper into a smooth pulp?
questions.explain: A mortar and pestle is commonly used in Nigerian practical art classes to pound soaked paper efficiently until it becomes a soft, uniform pulp.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Before mixing a binder (like starch) into the pounded paper pulp, an essential step is to:
options: Squeeze out the excess water from the pulp.
Boil the pulp over a high flame for an hour.
Add dry sand to thicken the mixture.
Paint the wet pulp with oil colors.
questions.explain: Excess water must be squeezed out of the pulp. If the pulp is too watery, the starch or glue will be diluted, and the resulting mixture will fail to hold its shape.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What is the function of cassava paste (starch) or glue in the preparation of paper mâché?
options: It gives the paper a sweet smell.
It acts as a binder to hold the paper particles firmly together.
It prevents the object from drying up.
It changes the color of the paper from white to brown.
questions.explain: A binder like cassava starch or paper glue is mixed with the pulp to act as an adhesive, ensuring that when the modeled object dries, it stays solid and strong.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following objects can be beautifully created using the paper mâché modelling technique?
questions.explain: Paper mâché is excellent for molding lightweight, rigid items such as decorative face masks, bowls, and piggy banks.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: When modelling a very large object with paper mâché, what is used to provide an internal framework or support structure?
questions.explain: An armature (usually made of wire, wood, or crushed paper/cardboard) is the internal framework used to support the wet paper mâché so it does not collapse under its own weight while drying.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: How should a newly modeled paper mâché object be treated to ensure it hardens properly?
options: It should be soaked in a bucket of clean water.
It should be left out to dry under the sun or in a well-ventilated space.
It should be immediately wrapped tightly in a plastic bag.
It should be placed in a freezer.
questions.explain: Paper mâché relies on the evaporation of water to harden. Drying it under the sun or in open air cures the binder, turning the pulp into a strong, rigid material.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: To achieve a smooth finish on a dried paper mâché object before painting, an artist would most likely use:
questions.explain: Sandpaper is used to gently rub off rough bumps and uneven textures on the surface of the dried paper mâché, creating a smooth surface ideal for painting.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What is the final stage in producing a paper mâché artwork, aimed at enhancing its beauty and protecting it?
questions.explain: Once dry and smooth, painting gives the object visual life, while varnishing provides a glossy, protective coat that makes it more durable and moisture-resistant.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: A major advantage of using paper mâché for school modeling projects over clay is that:
options: It requires firing in a very hot kiln.
It is heavily toxic and requires professional handling.
The materials (old newspapers and starch) are cheap and readily available.
The final product becomes heavier than metal.
questions.explain: Paper mâché is a highly accessible medium. Its primary components (waste paper and local starch) cost almost nothing and can be found easily, making it perfect for students.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: If a student attempts to model with paper mâché but the pulp easily crumbles and falls apart upon drying, what vital ingredient was likely left out?
questions.explain: The binder (like starch or glue) is the adhesive agent that holds the dry paper fibers together. Without it, the dried paper simply reverts to loose, crumbly pieces.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
